Name: Event Studio
Author: xzqute
Description:
[center][img width=600]https://i.imgur.com/SWFOR0p.png[/img][/center]

[size=4]Build a cutscene inside Stardew Valley: place Abigail beside your farmer, give her a route and a few lines, then watch the scene and export it as a Content Patcher pack. SVES also imports existing events, including the final event data loaded by other mods.[/size]

[size=5][b]Installation[/b][/size]

[size=4]SVES targets Stardew Valley 1.6.15 and SMAPI 4.5.x. The editor works in single-player. It is disabled in multiplayer, including when you host a co-op farm.[/size]

[list=1]
[*][size=4]Install [url=https://smapi.io/]SMAPI[/url] and follow its instructions for launching your game through SMAPI.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Download SVES from this page and extract the archive into your game's Mods folder. Keep the mod's files together in their own folder: manifest.json, StardewEventStudio.dll, StardewEventStudio.Core.dll, assets and i18n. Leaving the ZIP in Mods will not install it.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Launch through SMAPI and check that Stardew Valley Event Studio appears in the loaded-mod list. If SMAPI reports that it skipped the mod, resolve the reason shown in the console before continuing.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]To work from the main menu, click the studio's clapperboard button near the lower-left settings button. This opens a disposable studio world without loading one of your saves.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]To work in your own world, load a single-player save, finish any active event and press F10. You can also enter eventstudio in the SMAPI console, without a leading slash.[/size][/*]
[/list][size=4]In Steam, open the game's Properties, choose Installed Files, then Browse to find the game folder. Other installations may use a different path; look for the folder containing the game and Mods.[/size]

[size=4][url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/1915]Content Patcher[/url] is required to run the exported content pack. You can use the editor itself without it. Event Extensions and Event Command Codex are optional; install them if you want their commands, and connect them to your project as described below.[/size]

[size=5][b]Your first scene[/b][/size]

[size=4]Start with an NPC walking a few tiles toward the farmer and saying hello. Choose a clear patch of ground so you can concentrate on the sequence. The following sections explain the tools in sidebar order; these steps give you a complete first pass.[/size]

[list=1]
[*][size=4]Open the studio and choose New. In Scene, use Save As to give the project a recognizable filename.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]In Actors, choose + Add actor, search for Abigail and place her on a free tile. Return to the start with Home, then drag Abigail and farmer into their starting positions. Select Abigail and press F to cycle her facing.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]In Actions, find Move. Check that Abigail is the selected actor, pick a destination a few tiles away, and Apply. Leave Asynchronous off for this example.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Add Pause with a duration of 400 milliseconds. Add Dialogue, choose Abigail and enter "Hey, @! How are things on %farm?". Apply the dialogue draft.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Open Sequence and check that Move, Pause and Dialogue appear in that order. Select an action and use Ctrl+Up or Ctrl+Down to correct its position. Save the project.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Press Home, then Play or P to inspect the scene in Canvas. Run the project check and fix errors in Issues. Finally, use In game from a loaded save, or Native from the title-screen studio, to inspect real event playback.[/size][/*]
[/list][size=4]This gives you an editable scene and a preview. To make it start during normal gameplay, set its entry conditions and export a content pack using the instructions further down.[/size]

[size=5][b][img]https://i.imgur.com/QPe4SlE.png[/img] Scene[/b][/size]

[size=4]Choose the location, starting camera, initial music and scene environment. Set time, season and weather when you need to judge a conversation at dusk or check how a winter scene looks. These preview settings are separate from the conditions that trigger the finished event.[/size]

[size=4]Start with a new project for your own scene. Import a loaded event when you want to study or adapt something already installed; its data includes applied content patches. Raw script import is useful when you already have an event string. Unknown commands survive as Raw actions, though they may have no visual simulation.[/size]

[size=4]Pan and frame the editor camera to work comfortably, then set the event's starting camera deliberately. Grid and collision overlays help with placement. Keep current music is a useful starting choice while arranging the scene.[/size]

[center][img]https://i.imgur.com/FuWFo2Z.png[/img][/center]
[size=3][i]Scene setup and its environment controls. Staging presets are separate from event entry conditions.[/i][/size]

[size=5][b][img]https://i.imgur.com/g0JWE5v.png[/img] Actors[/b][/size]

[size=4]Add your farmer and choose NPCs from the character catalog. Search by display name or internal ID; loaded modded NPCs can appear too. Select an actor to edit its starting position, facing and outline color.[/size]

[size=4]At the start of the scene, drag Abigail onto a tile and turn her toward the farmer. Shift-click adds actors to the selection. Moving a selection together helps preserve a formation.[/size]

[size=4]Starting positions define where the event begins. To make Abigail walk over later, add a movement action. SVES records an absolute destination and compiles the relative movement required by the event engine. Check the route overlay for obstacles before adding dialogue at the destination.[/size]

[center][img]https://i.imgur.com/cLtsfna.png[/img][/center]
[size=3][i]Initial placement and Abigail's inspector. Add a Move action for movement later in the event.[/i][/size]

[size=5][b][img]https://i.imgur.com/fHn8hm0.png[/img] Actions[/b][/size]

[size=4]Pick an action, fill in its editor and Apply. Double-click its clip to revise it. The categories follow the sidebar order:[/size]

[list]
[*][size=4][b]Actors:[/b] choose poses, frames, animations and character presentation.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4][b]Move:[/b] walk, warp, turn or adjust movement behavior. Use a route when the character must go around an obstacle.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4][b]Talk:[/b] add spoken lines, messages and questions.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4][b]Scene:[/b] change the camera, location or map presentation.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4][b]Effects:[/b] add visual effects and temporary sprites.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4][b]Audio:[/b] choose sounds or music for a moment in the scene.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4][b]Story:[/b] author rewards and changes to game progress; check their preview behavior before testing.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4][b]Flow:[/b] control pauses, event flow and supported branching or extension blocks.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4][b]Lab:[/b] insert reusable actions saved in this project.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4][b]All:[/b] browse everything, or search when you know what you need.[/size][/*]
[/list][size=4]For a first scene, add a walk, a short pause and a spoken line. Tracks makes actor and command timing easy to inspect. Sequence is useful for reading the execution order and navigating nested blocks or branches.[/size]

[size=4]The timeline follows the event's ordered commands. Clip lengths visualize derived timing; they do not let every track run independently. Use supported simultaneous groups when actors should move together, and choose whether the group waits for movement to finish. A blocking vanilla move across both axes is compiled horizontally, then vertically. Vanilla asynchronous moves have stricter limits.[/size]

[center][img]https://i.imgur.com/IFYP0Zu.png[/img][/center]
[size=3][i]Action categories and the same scene's timeline. The sequence remains the execution order.[/i][/size]

[size=5][b][img]https://i.imgur.com/Wv6D2F9.png[/img] Text[/b][/size]

[size=4]Open a dialogue action to write its pages together. Choose each page's portrait expression from the available sheet and use the placeholder palette for the player's name, farm name and other vanilla substitutions. Gender variants have their own editor.[/size]

[size=4]An optional i18n key lets the exporter put the line into the pack's translation catalog. Reuse clear, unique keys as you write if you expect to translate the event. The interface's translation files and your event's dialogue translations are separate.[/size]

[size=4]Questions and forks are actions with their own answer and branch controls. Use them when the player's choice should change what happens next. A text placeholder alone does not create a branch. Canvas estimates reading time; the exported game's ordinary dialogue still waits for player input.[/size]

[center][img]https://i.imgur.com/Fwc9aeP.png[/img][/center]
[size=3][i]Dialogue with an i18n key, a portrait expression and atomic Player and Farm placeholders.[/i][/size]

[size=5][b][img]https://i.imgur.com/Uxu3zYi.png[/img] Lab[/b][/size]

[size=4]Turn a sequence you use repeatedly into one reusable action. For example, build a walk-and-greet sequence, expose its actor or destination as parameters, then insert it with different values elsewhere in the cutscene.[/size]

[size=4]Connect command nodes from Start to Finish and use compatible parameter connections to share values. Moving a card changes its layout; execution follows the connections. Lab has an independent test scene, so you can try a definition before inserting it into the main timeline.[/size]

[size=4]Definitions live inside the project. Editing a shared definition updates its instances in that project. You can also import or export a personal .svesaction library, or expand an instance back into ordinary actions. Exported packs need the commands' dependencies, with no separate Lab runtime. Lab reports invalid connections and cycles; it is not a general live game-state scripting environment.[/size]

[center][img]https://i.imgur.com/AisrPrK.png[/img][/center]
[size=3][i]Walk and greet as a reusable definition. Execution follows the wires from Start to Finish.[/i][/size]

[size=5][b][img]https://i.imgur.com/vgae2b3.png[/img] Issues[/b][/size]

[size=4]Run the project check before playback and export. Fix errors first: a missing actor, invalid field or broken Lab definition can stop the scene from compiling or playing. Then review warnings about routes, missing providers and unsupported preview behavior.[/size]

[size=4]An imported Raw command can still export correctly while having no Canvas representation. A clear Issues list also cannot guarantee another mod's runtime behavior. Test the installed pack after export, including the event's entry conditions and each relevant branch.[/size]

[center][img]https://i.imgur.com/Rt5ARTw.png[/img][/center]
[size=3][i]Deliberately broken example: the Move action refers to MissingActor. Repair the actor reference before playback.[/i][/size]

[size=5][b]Preview your scene[/b][/size]

[size=4][b]Canvas[/b] is the fast local simulation behind Play, scrubbing and stepping. Use it to adjust movement, camera work and dialogue placement. It models supported commands; dialogue durations and some other timings are estimates.[/size]

[size=4][b]In game[/b] from a loaded save uses the real event runtime with command-specific filtering and restoration. Blocked commands are replaced with advancing no-ops and reported in the log. Supported rewards and other sensitive behavior may use controlled preview handlers. Music uses a managed playback session: the compiled event starts with continue, and supported music changes are restored afterward.[/size]

[size=4][b]Native playback[/b] from the title-screen studio runs original commands in a disposable world and recreates that world afterward. Use it when you need to inspect behavior omitted by safe preview. Other mods still participate in that temporary session.[/size]

[size=4]Raw commands are skipped by default in save-backed preview. The optional Run Raw commands in game setting bypasses that default for Raw input; unknown third-party side effects have no general restoration guarantee. Prefer the disposable world for testing unfamiliar commands. Editing and preview are intended for single-player use.[/size]

[size=5][b]Save, conditions and export[/b][/size]

[size=4]Save keeps the editable .svesproject under the mod's projects folder. Open returns to saved work and recovery entries. Autosave and last-project reopening can be configured in Settings. Keep the source project when you publish a pack so you can revise it later.[/size]

[size=4]In Export, set the pack metadata and event ID, then open Conditions to choose when the event can start. For example, limit Abigail's conversation to evening and add a friendship requirement. Separate rules normally combine with AND; multiple seasons inside one season rule allow either season. Preview environment settings do not prove those entry rules work.[/size]

[size=4]Export a complete Content Patcher pack for a new mod, or event files and translations for an existing pack. Copy is useful when you want the generated script or patches on the clipboard. Exports go under the mod's exports folder. Install the finished pack with Content Patcher and any dependencies its commands require; the .svesproject file alone does not install an event.[/size]

[size=4]For your first standalone pack:[/size]

[list=1]
[*][size=4]Open Export and fill in Mod details: give the pack its own name, author, unique ID and version. Choose a distinct event ID in Conditions so it does not replace another author's event accidentally.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Add the entry rules you need. For an initial test, use conditions you can meet easily, then tighten them for publication.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]In the Export tab, choose Complete mod. Include the editable source if you want to distribute it with the pack, then export.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Open the new folder under exports. Copy the generated pack folder into your game's Mods folder, keeping its manifest.json and content.json together with the generated events and translations.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Install Content Patcher and any frameworks required by the pack. Restart through SMAPI, load a suitable save and enter the target location while the conditions are met. Check the SMAPI console if the event does not start.[/size][/*]
[/list][size=4]If you export event files for an existing mod, add their Include entries to that pack's content.json and merge the generated translation keys into its i18n files. Keep a copy of the existing pack before merging. For a new mod, Complete mod handles that structure for you.[/size]

[center][img]https://i.imgur.com/ZHihJv6.png[/img][/center]
[size=3][i]An evening Time window rule. Test the exported event's conditions in normal gameplay.[/i][/size]

[size=5][b]Optional event frameworks[/b][/size]

[size=4][b][url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/53331]Event Extensions[/url], by xzqute[/b], adds actor cloning and appearance controls, camera tools, scene effects and asynchronous operations. Use it for scenes that need transformed actors or effects beyond the vanilla controls. SVES integrates its commands with dedicated editors and Canvas support. The actorTint command requires Event Extensions 1.1.0 or newer.[/size]

[size=4][b][url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/53435]Event Command Codex[/url], by ichortower[/b], adds streams, conditional blocks, repeats, variables, pathfinding, queued camera and lighting changes, CGs and PlayerControl sequences. Use it for coordinated parallel activity or a scene where the player completes staged interactions. SVES includes an adapter for ECC 1.0.x with structured editing and bounded Canvas simulation; external conditions and interactions may need explicit test choices.[/size]

[size=4]Install the framework and connect it through the Extensions prompt or Export's Extensions tab. Installing a provider alone does not connect every existing project. Dependencies are inferred from emitted commands; you can also require a framework explicitly. Saved extension commands remain exportable without their provider, while editing and simulation may be unavailable. Players need each framework used by the exported pack.[/size]

[center][img]https://i.imgur.com/QOIOkwq.png[/img][/center]
[size=3][i]Saved framework connections in an offline project. These providers are not installed in this capture session.[/i][/size]

[size=5][b]Languages and workspace settings[/b][/size]

[size=4]The bundled interface is English. Its local Noto Sans font covers Latin, extended Latin, Cyrillic and common punctuation, including text such as café, Łódź and Привет. Glyph coverage does not mean those languages have complete interface translations. Additional UI translations can use SMAPI i18n files.[/size]

[size=4]CJK characters and complex-script shaping are unsupported; missing glyphs display as ?. The studio font does not replace the game's fonts, so check exported dialogue in the game language you intend to support.[/size]

[size=4]Settings offers Dark, Light, Tokyo Night and Parchment themes, accent colors and workflow options. Changes can be previewed before Apply.[/size]

[size=5][b]Keyboard and mouse controls[/b][/size]

[size=4]These controls depend on the active workspace and selection. Click out of a search field or finish the open form before using timeline shortcuts. While editing text, the input field handles typing and clipboard commands.[/size]

[size=4]In the main workspace:[/size]

[list]
[*][size=4]F10 opens or closes the studio and stops active runtime preview. This is the default OpenStudio keybind; config.json can change it.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Ctrl+S saves the project. Ctrl+Z undoes an edit; Ctrl+Y redoes it.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Ctrl+, opens Settings. Tab toggles Focus mode to give the scene more room.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]P plays or pauses Canvas. Home and End seek to the start and end. Left and Right step through actions in sequence order, including actions that share a timestamp.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Up and Down select the previous or next action. Enter edits the selected action.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Ctrl+C, Ctrl+X and Ctrl+V copy, cut and paste selected actions. Ctrl+D duplicates them; Ctrl+A selects all actions in the current timeline.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Ctrl+Up and Ctrl+Down move the selected actions earlier or later in the sequence.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Space enables or disables selected actions. Use P for playback.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]A toggles Asynchronous for selected Move actions outside simultaneous groups. Check movement limits before using it.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]F cycles the selected actor's initial facing. Delete removes selected actions, or selected actors together with their actions.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Escape cancels an active tool or drag, leaves Focus mode, or clears the action selection, depending on what is active. Open forms handle Escape as Cancel or Back.[/size][/*]
[/list][size=4]For scene placement and timeline navigation:[/size]

[list]
[*][size=4]Shift-click an actor or clip to add it to or remove it from the selection. At the scene's start, drag actors to change their initial positions.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Hold the middle mouse button and drag to pan the scene.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Over Tracks, use the wheel to scroll vertically, Shift+wheel to pan horizontally, and Ctrl+wheel to zoom around the pointer. In Sequence, the wheel scrolls the list.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Click or drag the timeline ruler to seek. Drag the timeline's upper edge to change its height.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Drag an action to a new insertion point to change sequence order. Moving clips does not create independent playback tracks.[/size][/*]
[/list][size=4]In the dialogue editor, Enter inserts a line break, Tab moves to the next page, and Ctrl+Enter applies the whole dialogue draft. Ctrl+A/C/X/V select, copy, cut and paste text; Shift with the arrow keys extends a selection. In resource lists, use Up/Down or Page Up/Page Down to browse and Enter to choose.[/size]

[size=4]Lab has its own controls while the graph is active:[/size]

[list]
[*][size=4]F fits the graph; Ctrl+F opens its search. P plays or pauses the test scene, Home stops it, and Left/Right step through it.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Ctrl+A selects nodes. Ctrl+C/V/D copy, paste and duplicate them; Delete removes selected nodes. Enter opens the selected command's editor.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]G groups compatible selected commands. Ctrl+Z/Ctrl+Y undo and redo Lab edits; Ctrl+S saves the project.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Drag empty graph space to select an area. Hold the middle mouse button to pan and use the wheel to zoom. Hold Alt while moving nodes for placement without grid snapping.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Ctrl-click a connected field input to disconnect it. Escape cancels an unfinished drag or connection and clears the graph selection.[/size][/*]
[/list][size=4]F turns an actor in the main workspace and fits the graph in Lab. G applies to Lab grouping; it is not a main-timeline grouping shortcut.[/size]

[size=5][b]Updating and removing SVES[/b][/size]

[size=4]Close the game before updating. Back up projects, exports and config.json from the installed SVES folder, replace the mod with the new version, and restore your working files if you replaced the entire folder. Keep one installed copy of SVES; two folders with the same mod UniqueID will cause a loading conflict.[/size]

[size=4]To remove the editor, close the game and remove its folder from Mods after keeping any projects you want. Exported packs installed elsewhere in Mods remain separate. Remove a pack as well if you want to disable its event. Removing a pack does not undo changes an event already made during normal gameplay.[/size]

[size=5][b]If something does not work[/b][/size]

[size=4]If the studio button or F10 does nothing, check that SMAPI loaded SVES, that you are in single-player, and that another event is not active. If an actor or map is missing, confirm the mod supplying it is installed and loaded in this session.[/size]

[size=4]If Canvas and real playback differ, check Issues and the preview log for omitted commands or estimated timing. Test unfamiliar Raw commands in the title-screen studio. If the exported event does not start, check its location, entry conditions, required frameworks and whether that save has already seen the event.[/size]

[size=4]When reporting a bug, include the SVES version, your [url=https://smapi.io/log]SMAPI log[/url], the steps that reproduce it, and whether it happened in Canvas, In game, Native or an installed pack. A small .svesproject that reproduces the problem makes an editor issue easier to investigate.[/size]

Downloads.Description: Added Event Command Codex integration with nested blocks, PlayerControl, preview, and export. Introduced Lab for visually creating, configuring, and testing reusable action blocks.
